questions.text: आसियान शैली मेल-मिलाप का एक ऐसा तरीका है जो _______ ।
questions.text_english: The ASEAN way of engagement is a style that is _______.
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) cooperative. The ASEAN way refers to a non-confrontational, informal, and consensus-based approach to diplomacy and regional problem-solving. ASEAN members prefer quiet diplomacy and consultation over formal, legally binding agreements or confrontational methods. Options A (formal), B (confrontationist), and D (provocative) are incorrect because ASEAN deliberately avoids rigid formalities and confrontation in its engagement style.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) सहयोगात्मक है। आसियान शैली एक अनौपचारिक, सर्वसम्मति-आधारित कूटनीतिक दृष्टिकोण है जो टकराव से बचती है और शांत वार्ता को प्राथमिकता देती है।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा देश आसियान का एक संस्थापक सदस्य नहीं है ?
questions.text_english: Which one of the following countries is not a founder-member of ASEAN ?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) Myanmar. ASEAN was founded in 1967 by five original members: Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, Singapore, and Thailand. Myanmar joined ASEAN much later in 1997. Therefore, Singapore (A), Thailand (B), and Indonesia (D) are all founding members, while Myanmar (C) is not.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) म्यांमार है। आसियान की स्थापना 1967 में इंडोनेशिया, मलेशिया, फिलीपींस, सिंगापुर और थाईलैंड द्वारा की गई थी। म्यांमार 1997 में आसियान में शामिल हुआ।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा देश दक्षिण एशिया में शामिल नहीं किया जाता है ?
questions.text_english: Which one of the following countries is not included in South Asia ?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) China. South Asia as a region typically includes India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Bhutan, Maldives, and Afghanistan. China is geographically located in East Asia, not South Asia. Bangladesh (A), Bhutan (C), and Maldives (D) are all recognized South Asian nations and members of SAARC.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) चीन है। दक्षिण एशिया में भारत, पाकिस्तान, बांग्लादेश, श्रीलंका, नेपाल, भूटान, मालदीव और अफगानिस्तान शामिल हैं। चीन पूर्वी एशिया का देश है।

questions.text: पाकिस्तान के निम्नलिखित शासकों को उनके शासन काल के आधार पर कालक्रमानुसार व्यवस्थित कीजिए : (i) जनरल ज़िया-उल-हक (ii) बेनज़ीर भुट्टो (iii) जनरल मुशर्रफ (iv) ज़ुल्फिकार अली भुट्टो
questions.text_english: Arrange the following rulers of Pakistan in the chronological order as per the period of their rule : (i) General Zia-ul-Haq (ii) Benazir Bhutto (iii) General Musharraf (iv) Zulfikar Ali Bhutto
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) (iv), (i), (ii), (iii). Zulfikar Ali Bhutto ruled Pakistan from 1971 to 1977. General Zia-ul-Haq then staged a coup and ruled from 1977 to 1988. Benazir Bhutto served as Prime Minister in two terms: 1988–1990 and 1993–1996. General Musharraf seized power in a coup in 1999 and ruled until 2008. This makes the correct chronological order: Zulfikar Ali Bhutto → Zia-ul-Haq → Benazir Bhutto → Musharraf.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा सुरक्षा का नया स्रोत नहीं माना जाता है ?
questions.text_english: Which one of the following is not considered as a new source of threat to security ?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) War. In contemporary security studies, 'new' sources of threat include terrorism, hijacking, use of drones for targeted attacks, cyber threats, environmental degradation, pandemics, and so on. War between states is considered a traditional or conventional source of security threat, not a new one. Therefore, terrorism (A), hijacking (B), and use of drones (C) are all classified as new/non-traditional threats, while war (D) is the odd one out as it is a traditional threat.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (D) युद्ध है। युद्ध एक पारंपरिक सुरक्षा खतरा है जबकि आतंकवाद, वायुयानों का अपहरण और ड्रोन का प्रयोग नए/गैर-पारंपरिक खतरे हैं।
questions.topic: New sources of threat to security

questions.text: अभिकथन (A) : गठबंधन में कई देश शामिल होते हैं जो सैन्य हमले को रोकने अथवा उससे रक्षा करने के लिए समवेत कदम उठाते हैं। कारण (R) : किसी अन्य देश अथवा गठबंधन की तुलना में अपनी प्रभावी शक्ति को बढ़ाने के लिए देश गठबंधन बनाते हैं।
questions.text_english: Assertion (A) : An alliance is a coalition of states that coordinate their actions to deter or defend against military attack. Reason (R) : Countries form alliances to increase their effective power relative to another country or alliance.
questions.instruction_line: दो कथन दिए गए हैं — एक को अभिकथन (A) और दूसरे को कारण (R) कहा गया है। इन कथनों को ध्यानपूर्वक पढ़िए और नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों (A), (B), (C) और (D) में से सही उत्तर चुनिए।
questions.instruction_line_english: For Question number 6, two statements are given one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Read these statements carefully and choose the correct option.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) गलत है, परन्तु कारण (R) सही है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) गलत है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (A). Both the Assertion and the Reason are true, and the Reason correctly explains the Assertion. An alliance is indeed a grouping of states that coordinate to deter or defend against military attack. The reason why countries form such alliances is precisely to enhance their effective power relative to a rival country or opposing alliance — making the Reason a direct and correct explanation of why alliances exist as described in the Assertion.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (A) है। अभिकथन और कारण दोनों सत्य हैं और कारण, अभिकथन की सही व्याख्या करता है। देश अपनी प्रभावी शक्ति बढ़ाने के लिए गठबंधन बनाते हैं जिससे वे सैन्य हमलों को रोक सकें।
questions.topic: Alliance formation and balance of power

questions.text: 1950 के दशक के दौरान भारत और अमेरिका के संबंधों में काफी तनाव था क्योंकि :
questions.text_english: There was considerable unease in Indo-US relations during the 1950s because :

options.A: भारत के सोवियत संघ के साथ संबंध बढ़ रहे थे।
options.B: सोवियत संघ ने हंगरी पर आक्रमण कर दिया।
options.C: भारत नाटो (NATO) का एक सदस्य नहीं था।
options.D: भारत गुट निरपेक्ष आंदोलन (NAM) का संस्थापक सदस्य था।

options_english.A: India had a growing partnership with the Soviet Union.
options_english.C: India was not a member of NATO.
options_english.D: India was a founder member of NAM.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (D). During the 1950s, Indo-US relations were strained primarily because India was a founding member of the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM). The United States, in the context of the Cold War, expected countries to align with one bloc or the other. India's insistence on staying non-aligned and not joining Western alliances like NATO or SEATO caused considerable unease in Washington. Option A describes a later development, option B relates to Soviet actions, and option C is a factual statement that does not explain the tension.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (D) है। 1950 के दशक में भारत के गुट निरपेक्ष आंदोलन का संस्थापक सदस्य होने से अमेरिका के साथ संबंध तनावपूर्ण रहे क्योंकि शीतयुद्ध के दौरान अमेरिका सभी देशों से किसी न किसी गुट में शामिल होने की अपेक्षा रखता था।
questions.chapter: US Hegemony in World Politics / Non-Aligned Movement

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा एक जवाहरलाल नेहरू की विदेश नीति का प्रमुख लक्ष्य नहीं था ?
questions.text_english: Which one of the following was not a major objective of Jawaharlal Nehru's foreign policy ?

options.A: कठिन संघर्ष से प्राप्त भारत की संप्रभुता को बचाए रखना।
options.B: भारत की क्षेत्रीय अखंडता की रक्षा करना।
options.C: भारत को एक परमाणु शक्ति बनाना।
options.D: तीव्र आर्थिक विकास को बढ़ावा देना।

options_english.A: To preserve the hard-earned sovereignty of India.
options_english.B: To protect the territorial integrity of India.
options_english.C: To make India a nuclear power.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (C). Making India a nuclear power was not a major objective of Nehru's foreign policy. In fact, Nehru was a firm advocate of nuclear disarmament and peaceful uses of atomic energy. He opposed nuclear weapons proliferation. His foreign policy goals centered on preserving India's sovereignty (A), protecting territorial integrity (B), and promoting rapid economic development (D) through planned development. India conducted its first nuclear test only in 1974 under Indira Gandhi, years after Nehru's death.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) है। नेहरू की विदेश नीति का उद्देश्य भारत को परमाणु शक्ति बनाना नहीं था। वे परमाणु निरस्त्रीकरण के समर्थक थे। भारत का पहला परमाणु परीक्षण 1974 में इंदिरा गांधी के नेतृत्व में हुआ।
questions.chapter: Era of One-Party Dominance / Nehru's Foreign Policy

questions.text: लाल बहादुर शास्त्री से संबंधित, निम्नलिखित कथनों में से गलत कथन की पहचान कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Identify the false statement from the following related to Lal Bahadur Shastri.

options.A: वर्ष 1966 तक उन्होंने कांग्रेस पार्टी के महासचिव के रूप में कार्य किया।
options.B: वे तीन वर्ष के अल्पकाल के लिए संघीय मंत्रिमंडल के सदस्य रहे।
options.C: एक रेल दुर्घटना का दायित्व अपने पर लेते हुए, उन्होंने संघीय मंत्रिमंडल से त्यागपत्र दे दिया था।
options.D: जय जवान जय किसान उनका प्रसिद्ध नारा था।

options_english.A: He worked as the General Secretary of the Congress Party till 1966.
options_english.B: He was in the Union Cabinet for a short period of three years.
options_english.C: He resigned from the Union Cabinet taking responsibility for a Railway accident.
options_english.D: Jai Jawan Jai Kisan was his famous slogan.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (A), which is the false statement. Lal Bahadur Shastri did not work as General Secretary of the Congress Party till 1966. He became Prime Minister of India in 1964 after the death of Nehru and served until his own death in January 1966 in Tashkent. He did resign from the Union Cabinet taking responsibility for a railway accident (C is true), 'Jai Jawan Jai Kisan' was indeed his famous slogan (D is true), and statement B is also historically accurate.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (A) है जो कि गलत कथन है। शास्त्री जी 1964 में प्रधानमंत्री बने और 1966 में ताशकंद में उनका निधन हुआ। वे 1966 तक कांग्रेस महासचिव के रूप में नहीं रहे।

questions.text: भारत में चौथे आम चुनाव से पूर्व निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सी समस्याएँ थीं ? (i) मानसून की असफलता (ii) खाद्य संकट (iii) अधिक वर्षा (iv) विदेशी मुद्रा-भंडार में कमी
questions.text_english: Which of the following problems did India face before the 4th general elections ? (i) Failure of monsoon (ii) Food crisis (iii) Heavy rainfall (iv) Depletion of foreign exchange reserves
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) — (i), (ii), and (iv). Before the fourth general elections of 1967, India faced a severe failure of monsoon leading to drought conditions, an acute food crisis that required large-scale food imports, and a significant depletion of foreign exchange reserves. Heavy rainfall (iii) was not a problem during this period; rather, the crisis was caused by inadequate rains. These combined challenges severely tested the Indian state and contributed to Congress losing its majority in several states in 1967.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) है। 1967 के चौथे आम चुनावों से पूर्व भारत में मानसून की विफलता, खाद्य संकट और विदेशी मुद्रा भंडार में कमी की समस्याएँ थीं। अधिक वर्षा (iii) इस काल की समस्या नहीं थी।

questions.text: भारत के निम्नलिखित प्रधानमंत्रियों को उनके कार्यकाल के आधार पर कालक्रमानुसार व्यवस्थित कीजिए : (i) एच.डी. देवे (ii) चंद्र शेखर (iii) पी.वी. नरसिम्हा राव (iv) वी.पी. सिंह
questions.text_english: Arrange the following Prime Ministers of India in the chronological order as per their period of rule : (i) H.D. Deve Gowda (ii) Chandra Shekhar (iii) P.V. Narsimha Rao (iv) V.P. Singh
questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) — (iv), (ii), (iii), (i). V.P. Singh became Prime Minister in December 1989 after the 1989 elections. Chandra Shekhar succeeded him in November 1990. P.V. Narasimha Rao became PM after the 1991 elections and served till 1996. H.D. Deve Gowda became PM in June 1996 as head of the United Front government. The correct chronological order is therefore: V.P. Singh → Chandra Shekhar → P.V. Narasimha Rao → H.D. Deve Gowda.
questions.chapter: Rise of Popular Movements / Coalition Politics
questions.topic: Chronological order of Prime Ministers of India

questions.text: सूची-I का सूची-II से सही मिलान कीजिए और सही विकल्प चुनिए :
questions.text_english: Match List-I with the List-II and choose the correct option :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A): 1-(iv), 2-(i), 3-(ii), 4-(iii). The BJP-led National Democratic Alliance (NDA) won a clear majority in the 17th Lok Sabha (2019). The Mandal Commission recommendations were implemented by the V.P. Singh-led National Front Government (1989-90). H.D. Deve Gowda headed the United Front Government (1996-97). Prime Minister Manmohan Singh led the United Progressive Alliance (UPA) Government (2004-2014). This makes option A the only correct match for all four items.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (A) है: 1-(iv) NDA, 2-(i) राष्ट्रीय मोर्चा, 3-(ii) संयुक्त मोर्चा, 4-(iii) UPA। NDA को 17वीं लोक सभा में स्पष्ट बहुमत मिला, मंडल आयोग की सिफारिशें राष्ट्रीय मोर्चा सरकार ने लागू कीं।

questions.text: पाकिस्तान में स्थायी लोकतंत्र की स्थापना में असफलता के लिए उत्तरदायी किन्हीं दो कारकों की व्याख्या कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Explain any two factors responsible for the failure in building a stable democracy in Pakistan.

key_points: Role of the military — the army has repeatedly intervened in civilian governance and staged coups, preventing the consolidation of democratic institutions.
Weak political institutions and dominance of feudal and tribal elites who resist democratic accountability and rule of law.

questions.solution: Two major factors have hindered the establishment of stable democracy in Pakistan. First, the dominant role of the military has repeatedly undermined civilian governments. The army has staged multiple coups — under Ayub Khan, Yahya Khan, Zia-ul-Haq, and Pervez Musharraf — weakening democratic norms and institutions. Second, Pakistan's political structure is dominated by feudal landlords and tribal elites who resist genuine democratic participation. These powerful groups prioritize personal and clan interests over constitutional governance, making it difficult for democracy to take root at the grassroots level.
questions.solution_hindi: पाकिस्तान में लोकतंत्र की विफलता के दो प्रमुख कारण हैं: प्रथम, सेना की प्रभावशाली भूमिका — अयूब खान, याह्या खान, जिया-उल-हक व मुशर्रफ जैसे सैन्य तानाशाहों ने बार-बार सत्ता पर कब्जा किया। द्वितीय, सामंती और कबायली कुलीन वर्ग का वर्चस्व जो वास्तविक लोकतांत्रिक भागीदारी को रोकता है।

questions.text: बांग्लादेश के संविधान की किन्हीं दो विशेषताओं को उजागर कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Highlight any two features of the Constitution of Bangladesh.

key_points: Bangladesh's 1972 Constitution declared the country a secular, democratic republic with a parliamentary form of government.
It enshrined socialism as one of the fundamental state principles, alongside nationalism, democracy, and secularism.

questions.solution: The Constitution of Bangladesh, adopted in 1972, has two notable features. First, it established Bangladesh as a parliamentary democracy with a secular character, guaranteeing fundamental rights to all citizens regardless of religion or ethnicity. Second, the constitution was founded on four state principles — nationalism, socialism, democracy, and secularism — reflecting the ideals of the liberation movement. Although later amendments modified secularism and introduced Islam as the state religion under military rulers, the original constitution remained a landmark democratic document.
questions.solution_hindi: बांग्लादेश के 1972 के संविधान की दो विशेषताएँ: प्रथम, यह एक धर्मनिरपेक्ष, लोकतांत्रिक गणराज्य की स्थापना करता है जिसमें संसदीय शासन प्रणाली है। द्वितीय, इसमें राष्ट्रवाद, समाजवाद, लोकतंत्र और धर्मनिरपेक्षता को राज्य के चार मूल सिद्धांतों के रूप में स्थापित किया गया।

questions.text: संयुक्त राष्ट्र संघ जैसे अंतर्राष्ट्रीय संगठनों के कोई दो लाभ लिखिए।
questions.text_english: State any two advantages of international organisations like the UNO.

key_points: International organisations like the UN provide a global forum for peaceful resolution of disputes and prevent conflicts from escalating into wars.
They coordinate international cooperation on global issues like health, climate change, poverty, and human rights where no single country can act alone.

questions.solution: International organisations like the United Nations serve two crucial purposes. First, they provide a multilateral forum where nations can resolve disputes peacefully through dialogue, negotiation, and arbitration, thereby reducing the risk of armed conflict. The UN Security Council and the International Court of Justice are examples of such mechanisms. Second, international organisations enable global coordination on shared challenges such as climate change, poverty, disease, and human rights, which no single nation can address independently. The UN's specialised agencies like WHO, UNICEF, and UNESCO exemplify this cooperative role.
questions.solution_hindi: UNO जैसे संगठनों के दो लाभ: प्रथम, वे देशों को शांतिपूर्ण ढंग से विवादों को सुलझाने का मंच प्रदान करते हैं। द्वितीय, जलवायु परिवर्तन, गरीबी व स्वास्थ्य जैसी वैश्विक समस्याओं के समाधान में अंतर्राष्ट्रीय सहयोग को बढ़ावा देते हैं।

questions.text: द्वितीय पंचवर्षीय योजना का मुख्य योजनाकार कौन था ? द्वितीय पंचवर्षीय योजना में किस बात पर बल दिया गया ?
questions.text_english: Who was the main architect of the Second Five Year Plan ? What did the Second Five Year Plan stress upon ?

key_points: P.C. Mahalanobis was the main architect of the Second Five Year Plan (1956-61).
The Second Five Year Plan stressed upon rapid industrialisation with a focus on heavy industries in the public sector.

questions.solution: The main architect of the Second Five Year Plan (1956–1961) was Professor P.C. Mahalanobis, a renowned statistician and economist. The Mahalanobis Model, as it came to be known, placed primary emphasis on the rapid development of heavy and basic industries such as steel, coal, and machinery. The plan stressed the importance of expanding the public sector and reducing India's dependence on imported goods by building a strong domestic industrial base, following a socialist pattern of development.
questions.solution_hindi: द्वितीय पंचवर्षीय योजना (1956-61) के मुख्य योजनाकार प्रोफेसर पी.सी. महालनोबिस थे। इस योजना में भारी उद्योगों के विकास पर विशेष बल दिया गया। सार्वजनिक क्षेत्र के विस्तार को प्राथमिकता दी गई।

questions.text: राजनीति में दल-बदल शब्द के अर्थ की व्याख्या कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Explain the meaning of the term 'defection' in politics.

key_points: Defection in politics refers to the act of an elected representative leaving the political party on whose ticket they were elected in order to join another party.
This practice became so rampant in India after 1967 that it was popularly called 'Aaya Ram Gaya Ram' politics and led to political instability.

questions.solution: In politics, 'defection' refers to the practice whereby an elected legislator abandons the political party on whose ticket they contested and won the election, and joins a rival political party, often for personal gain or ministerial office. In India, this phenomenon became widespread after the 1967 elections and was mockingly called 'Aaya Ram Gaya Ram' politics. It led to frequent changes of government and political instability. To control this, the Anti-Defection Law was enacted through the 52nd Constitutional Amendment in 1985.
questions.solution_hindi: राजनीति में दल-बदल का अर्थ है — किसी निर्वाचित विधायक या सांसद का अपने चुनाव चिह्न (पार्टी) को छोड़कर किसी अन्य दल में शामिल होना। 1967 के बाद भारत में यह प्रवृत्ति बहुत बढ़ गई जिसे 'आया राम गया राम' की राजनीति कहा जाने लगा। इस पर नियंत्रण के लिए 1985 में दल-बदल विरोधी कानून बनाया गया।

questions.text: भारतीय राजनीति में वर्ष 1989 से 2014 के कालखंड की तुलना में 2014 के बाद आए किन्हीं दो परिवर्तनों को स्पष्ट कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Explain any two changes that came in Indian politics after 2014 as compared to the period 1989 to 2014.

key_points: End of coalition compulsion: After 2014, the BJP achieved a clear single-party majority in the Lok Sabha, ending the era of coalition dependency that had defined 1989-2014.
Consolidation of BJP as the dominant party at the national level, replacing the Congress-dominated political landscape and shifting the ideological discourse of Indian politics.

questions.solution: Two significant changes emerged in Indian politics after 2014. First, the era of fragile coalition governments came to an end. Between 1989 and 2014, no single party won an outright majority, making coalition politics the norm. After the 2014 elections, the BJP secured a clear majority on its own, marking a decisive shift towards single-party dominance. Second, the BJP emerged as the new dominant party at the national level, replacing the Congress-led political order. This represented a major ideological shift in Indian politics, with the focus moving from coalition-based governance to a more centralised form of government.
questions.solution_hindi: 2014 के बाद भारतीय राजनीति में दो प्रमुख परिवर्तन आए: प्रथम, 1989-2014 के गठबंधन युग का अंत हुआ और भाजपा ने अकेले स्पष्ट बहुमत प्राप्त किया। द्वितीय, कांग्रेस की प्रधानता समाप्त होकर भाजपा राष्ट्रीय स्तर की प्रमुख पार्टी के रूप में उभरी।

questions.text: (क) यूरोपीय संघ के आर्थिक महत्त्व का आकलन कीजिए। अथवा (ख) अधिराष्ट्रीय संगठन के तौर पर यूरोपीय संघ की भूमिका का उदाहरणों की सहायता से विश्लेषण कीजिए।
questions.text_english: (a) Assess the economic importance of the European Union. OR (b) Analyse the role of the European Union as a supranational organisation with the help of examples.

sub_questions.text: यूरोपीय संघ के आर्थिक महत्त्व का आकलन कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Assess the economic importance of the European Union.

key_points: The EU is the world's largest single market with free movement of goods, services, capital, and people.
The euro, the common currency, simplifies trade and reduces transaction costs among member states.
The EU collectively is the world's largest trading bloc and a major source of foreign direct investment.
It has significant economic leverage in setting global trade rules and negotiating trade agreements.

sub_questions.solution: The European Union holds immense economic importance in global politics. As the world's largest single market, it allows the free movement of goods, services, capital, and labour across its member states, creating unparalleled economic integration. The euro, adopted as a common currency by 19 member states, eliminates exchange rate risks and facilitates easier trade. Economically, the EU as a bloc rivals the United States and China in terms of GDP and trade volume. It is the world's largest trading entity, accounting for a significant portion of global imports and exports. The EU also plays a dominant role in setting international trade regulations and norms, and its monetary policy, controlled by the European Central Bank, influences global financial markets. This collective economic strength gives individual member states far greater international bargaining power than they would have alone.

sub_questions.text: अधिराष्ट्रीय संगठन के तौर पर यूरोपीय संघ की भूमिका का उदाहरणों की सहायता से विश्लेषण कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Analyse the role of the European Union as a supranational organisation with the help of examples.

key_points: The EU acts as a supranational body where member states transfer some sovereignty to common EU institutions.
The European Parliament legislates on behalf of all member nations on matters covered by EU treaties.
The European Court of Justice adjudicates disputes between member states and EU institutions, and its rulings override national laws.
The European Central Bank sets monetary policy for eurozone members, overriding individual national central banks.

sub_questions.solution: The European Union functions as a supranational organisation because its member states have voluntarily transferred significant aspects of their sovereignty to common EU institutions, which can make decisions binding on all members. The European Parliament, directly elected by citizens of member nations, legislates on a wide range of issues including trade, environment, and consumer protection. The European Court of Justice adjudicates disputes and its rulings are binding on all member states — for example, it has overruled national laws that conflicted with EU regulations. The European Central Bank sets monetary policy for the eurozone, overriding the authority of individual national central banks. The EU also speaks with a unified voice in international trade negotiations, as seen in its trade deals with India, Canada, and the USA. These examples demonstrate how the EU transcends the status of a mere intergovernmental organisation.

questions.solution: This question has two internal choice options. Answers are provided under sub_questions (a) and (b).
questions.topic: Role and economic importance of EU

questions.text: संयुक्त राष्ट्र सुरक्षा परिषद के नए स्थायी एवं अस्थायी सदस्यों के लिए 1997 में प्रस्तावित किन्हीं चार मानदंडों का वर्णन कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Describe any four criteria proposed in 1997 for new permanent and non-permanent members of the UN Security Council.

key_points: A country should be a major contributor to the UN budget.
It should have a large population and a significant economic size.
It should respect democracy and human rights.
It should be militarily capable of contributing to UN peacekeeping operations.

questions.solution: In 1997, the Razali Report proposed specific criteria for selecting new permanent and non-permanent members of the UN Security Council. First, a candidate country should make substantial financial contributions to the United Nations budget, demonstrating commitment to the organisation. Second, the country should have a large population, ensuring that the reformed Council represents the majority of the world's people. Third, it should have a significant economic size and potential to contribute to global economic governance. Fourth, the country should have a demonstrated commitment to democracy and human rights, consistent with the UN's founding values. A fifth criterion also proposed was military capability, particularly the ability to contribute meaningfully to UN peacekeeping missions around the world.
questions.solution_hindi: 1997 में प्रस्तावित चार मानदंड: (1) UN बजट में पर्याप्त योगदान, (2) बड़ी जनसंख्या व आर्थिक आकार, (3) लोकतंत्र और मानवाधिकारों के प्रति प्रतिबद्धता, (4) UN शांति अभियानों में सैन्य योगदान की क्षमता।

questions.text: (क) मानव सुरक्षा का प्राथमिक लक्ष्य क्या है ? मानवता की सुरक्षा के संकीर्ण तथा व्यापक दृष्टिकोण में अंतर स्पष्ट कीजिए। अथवा (ख) एशिया तथा अफ्रीका के नए स्वतंत्र देशों के समज आईं सुरक्षा चुनौतियों की व्याख्या कीजिए।
questions.text_english: (a) What is the primary goal of human security ? Explain the difference between the narrow and broad concepts of human security. OR (b) Explain the security challenges faced by the newly independent countries of Asia and Africa.

sub_questions.text: मानव सुरक्षा का प्राथमिक लक्ष्य क्या है ? मानवता की सुरक्षा के संकीर्ण तथा व्यापक दृष्टिकोण में अंतर स्पष्ट कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: What is the primary goal of human security ? Explain the difference between the narrow and broad concepts of human security.

key_points: The primary goal of human security is to protect individual human beings from violence, fear, and want.
The narrow concept focuses specifically on protecting people from violent conflicts and armed attacks.
The broad concept encompasses freedom from hunger, disease, poverty, and environmental degradation in addition to violent threats.
The broader view was articulated by the UN Development Programme's Human Development Report 1994.

sub_questions.solution: The primary goal of human security is to protect individual human beings from all forms of threats — not merely interstate wars — that endanger their lives and dignity. The narrow concept of human security focuses specifically on protecting civilians from the violence of armed conflict, genocide, and state repression. It emphasises the physical safety of people from organised violence. The broad concept, developed notably by the UNDP's Human Development Report (1994), goes further to include freedom from hunger, poverty, disease, environmental degradation, and human rights violations. It argues that security cannot be achieved simply by protecting people from bullets; they must also be protected from the structural violence of poverty and disease. In short, the narrow view is conflict-centric while the broader view is centred on overall human well-being.

sub_questions.text: एशिया तथा अफ्रीका के नए स्वतंत्र देशों के समक्ष आईं सुरक्षा चुनौतियों की व्याख्या कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Explain the security challenges faced by the newly independent countries of Asia and Africa.

key_points: Threat from former colonial powers seeking to maintain influence.
Internal conflicts due to arbitrary colonial-era borders that grouped rival ethnic or religious communities together.
Lack of democratic institutions, military coups, and authoritarian rule.
Poverty, underdevelopment, and economic dependence on former colonial powers.

sub_questions.solution: Newly independent countries of Asia and Africa faced several interrelated security challenges after decolonisation. First, many faced the threat of external interference from former colonial powers that were reluctant to give up economic and strategic control. Second, colonial-era borders, drawn arbitrarily without respect for ethnic, linguistic, or religious communities, led to severe internal conflicts. Countries like Nigeria, Rwanda, and the Democratic Republic of Congo suffered devastating civil wars as a result. Third, the absence of democratic traditions and weak institutions left many states vulnerable to military coups and authoritarian regimes. Fourth, endemic poverty, economic underdevelopment, and dependence on a single commodity export made these nations economically fragile, creating conditions for social unrest and violence.

questions.solution: This question has two internal choice options. Answers are provided under sub_questions (a) and (b).
questions.topic: Human security / Security challenges in Asia and Africa

questions.text: लोकतंत्र में राजनीति की महत्त्वपूर्ण भूमिका को ध्यान में रखते हुए हमारे राष्ट्रीय नेताओं ने नव स्वतंत्र भारत के लिए किस मार्ग को अपनाया ? किन्हीं दो बिंदुओं को स्पष्ट कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Keeping in mind the crucial role of politics in a democracy, which route did our national leaders decide to take in the newly independent India ? Explain any two points.

key_points: India chose to maintain democratic politics and universal adult franchise, trusting ordinary citizens with the right to vote despite widespread poverty and illiteracy.
National leaders chose to preserve unity and integrity through a federal democratic structure rather than authoritarian centralisation, accommodating the diversity of India.

questions.solution: India's national leaders, recognising the centrality of democratic politics, chose a distinctive path for the newly independent nation. First, they decided to uphold universal adult franchise and democratic elections despite widespread illiteracy and poverty. Many sceptics doubted whether ordinary Indians could exercise informed choices, but leaders like Nehru and Ambedkar firmly believed that democracy was the only legitimate basis for governance. Second, they chose to accommodate India's enormous religious, linguistic, and cultural diversity through a federal democratic framework rather than imposing a uniform, centralised, authoritarian structure. This meant that regional aspirations could be expressed within a democratic framework, preserving national unity while respecting plurality. These choices made Indian democracy a remarkable experiment in the world.
questions.solution_hindi: भारत के राष्ट्रीय नेताओं ने दो मार्ग चुने: प्रथम, व्यापक गरीबी और अशिक्षा के बावजूद सार्वभौम वयस्क मताधिकार को बनाए रखा। द्वितीय, भारत की विविधता को संरक्षित करने के लिए संघीय लोकतांत्रिक ढाँचा अपनाया गया।
questions.topic: Democratic route chosen by India's national leaders

questions.text: भारत की विदेश नीति में जवाहरलाल नेहरू की भूमिका उजागर कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Highlight the role of Jawaharlal Nehru in the foreign policy of India.

key_points: Nehru was the principal architect of India's foreign policy and served as both Prime Minister and Foreign Minister.
He established the doctrine of Non-Alignment, keeping India independent from both the US-led and Soviet-led blocs.
He championed Panchsheel — the five principles of peaceful coexistence — as the basis for India's international relations.
He promoted Afro-Asian solidarity and was a driving force behind the 1955 Bandung Conference.

questions.solution: Jawaharlal Nehru was the principal architect of independent India's foreign policy, holding the portfolios of both Prime Minister and External Affairs Minister. He envisioned a policy of Non-Alignment, refusing to join either the American or Soviet bloc during the Cold War. This allowed India to maintain its sovereignty and pursue independent foreign policy decisions. Nehru championed the five principles of Panchsheel — peaceful coexistence, mutual non-aggression, non-interference, equality, and peaceful relations — as the foundation of India's international relations, first signed with China in 1954. He also promoted Afro-Asian solidarity and played a key role in the 1955 Bandung Conference, which gave rise to the Non-Aligned Movement formally established in 1961. Nehru's vision shaped India's global image as a peaceful, independent voice in world affairs.
questions.solution_hindi: नेहरू भारत की विदेश नीति के प्रमुख शिल्पकार थे। उन्होंने गुट निरपेक्षता की नीति अपनाई, पंचशील सिद्धांतों को विकसित किया, एशिया-अफ्रीका एकजुटता को बढ़ावा दिया और बांडुंग सम्मेलन (1955) में महत्त्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाई।
questions.chapter: Era of One-Party Dominance / Nehru's Foreign Policy
questions.topic: Nehru's role in India's foreign policy

questions.text: निम्नलिखित अवतरण को ध्यानपूर्वक पढ़िए और नीचे दिए गए प्रश्नों के उत्तर दीजिए : वैश्वीकरण एक बहुआयामी अवधारणा है। इसके अनेक आयाम हैं और उनके बीच ठीक-ठीक भेद किया जाना चाहिए। यह मान लेना गलत है कि वैश्वीकरण का केवल एक आयाम है। ठीक इसी तरह, यह मान लेना भी भूल होगी कि वैश्वीकरण एकदम सांस्कृतिक परिघटना है। वैश्वीकरण का प्रभाव बहुआयामी रहा है; यह कुछ समाजों को बाकी की अपेक्षा अधिक प्रभावित करता है। ऐसे में ज़रूरी हो जाता है कि विशिष्ट संदर्भों पर पर्याप्त ध्यान दिए बिना, हम वैश्वीकरण के प्रभाव के बारे में सर्व-सामान्य निष्कर्ष निकालने से परहेज करें।
questions.text_english: Globalisation is a multi-dimensional concept. It has various manifestations, and these must be adequately distinguished. It is wrong to assume that globalisation has only one dimension, just as it would also be mistaken to assume that it is a purely cultural phenomenon. The impact of globalisation is multi-dimensional; it affects some societies more than others and it is important to avoid drawing general conclusions about the impact of globalisation without paying sufficient attention to specific contexts.

sub_questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा आयाम, वैश्वीकरण का आयाम नहीं है ?
sub_questions.text_english: Which one of the following is not a dimension of globalisation ?
sub_questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) Ethical. Globalisation is generally described as having political, economic, cultural, and technological dimensions. 'Ethical' is not a standard recognised dimension of globalisation as described in the passage or in political science literature. The passage itself mentions that it would be wrong to think globalisation is purely cultural (C), and economic (D) and political (A) dimensions are widely acknowledged.

sub_questions.text: वैश्वीकरण से संबंधित निम्नलिखित कथनों में से कौन-सा सही नहीं है ?
sub_questions.text_english: Which one of the following statements related to globalisation is not correct ?

options.A: प्रौद्योगिकीय, पूंजी, वस्तुओं और लोगों के प्रवाह में पर्याप्त सहायक होती है।
options.B: वैश्वीकरण विभिन्न देशों की संस्कृतियों को प्रभावित करता है।
options.C: यह संपूर्ण विश्व को समान रूप से प्रभावित करता है।
options.D: जब प्रमुख आर्थिक घटनाएँ घटती हैं, तो उनका प्रभाव वैश्विक स्तर पर महसूस किया जाता है।

options_english.A: The technological advances do help a lot in the flow of ideas, capital, commodities and people.
options_english.B: Globalisation affects the cultures of different countries.
options_english.C: It affects all over the world equally.
options_english.D: When major economic events take place, their impact is felt at the global level.

sub_questions.solution: The correct answer is (C). The passage explicitly states that globalisation 'affects some societies more than others' — meaning it does not affect the entire world equally. Therefore, the claim that 'it affects all over the world equally' is incorrect and contradicts the passage directly. Options A, B, and D are all accurate statements about globalisation.

sub_questions.text: एक अवधारणा के रूप में वैश्वीकरण निम्नलिखित में से किस एक के साथ संबंधित नहीं है ?
sub_questions.text_english: Globalisation as a concept does not deal with which one of the following ?
sub_questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) Flow of rivers. Globalisation as a concept relates to the cross-border movement of ideas (A), capital (B), commodities, and people (D). The flow of rivers is a natural geographical phenomenon and has no connection to globalisation as a social, economic, or political concept.

sub_questions.text: वैश्वीकरण का प्रभाव प्रायः कैसा होता है ?
sub_questions.text_english: The impact of globalisation is vastly ___________.
sub_questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) uneven. The passage clearly states that 'the impact of globalisation is multi-dimensional; it affects some societies more than others.' This directly indicates that the impact of globalisation is uneven — not equal across all societies and regions. 'Discriminatory' (C) implies intentional bias, and 'regional' (D) is too narrow, so (B) uneven is the best match for what the passage describes.

questions.solution: Passage-based question set on globalisation. Answers are provided in sub_questions (i) through (iv).

questions.text: भारत के दिए गए राजनीतिक रेखा-मानचित्र (पृष्ठ 15 पर), में चार राज्यों को A, B, C और D के द्वारा अंकित किया गया है। नीचे दी गई जानकारी के आधार पर इन राज्यों की पहचान कीजिए और अपनी उत्तर-पुस्तिका में इनके सही नाम, प्रयोग की गई जानकारी की क्रम-संख्या तथा मानचित्र में दिया गया संबंधित अक्षर, नीचे दी गई तालिका के रूप में लिखिए।
questions.text_english: In the given political outline map of India (on page 17), four States have been marked as A, B, C, and D. Identify these States on the basis of the information given below and write their correct names in your answer-book along with the respective serial number of the information used and the concerned alphabets given in the map.
questions.instruction_line: (i) वह राज्य जिससे पूर्व प्रधानमंत्री चौधरी चरण सिंह संबंधित थे। (ii) वह राज्य जिससे पूर्व उप-प्रधानमंत्री जगजीवन राम संबंधित थे। (iii) वह राज्य जहाँ नक्सली सबसे अधिक सक्रिय थे। (iv) एक राज्य जहाँ से कांग्रेस पार्टी 1977 के लोक सभा चुनावों में एक भी सीट नहीं जीत पाई थी।
questions.instruction_line_english: (i) The State related to former Prime Minister Chaudhary Charan Singh. (ii) The State to which former Deputy Prime Minister Jagjivan Ram belonged. (iii) The State where the Naxalites were very active. (iv) A State where the Congress party could not win even a single seat in the Lok Sabha elections in 1977.

key_points: (i) A = Uttar Pradesh — Chaudhary Charan Singh was associated with Uttar Pradesh.
(ii) C = Bihar — Jagjivan Ram was associated with Bihar.
(iii) B = West Bengal — Naxalites were very active in West Bengal (Naxalbari movement originated here).
(iv) D = Uttar Pradesh or Rajasthan — Congress failed to win a single seat in states like Uttar Pradesh in 1977.

questions.solution: Based on the map markings and the information given: (i) Marker A represents Uttar Pradesh, which was associated with former Prime Minister Chaudhary Charan Singh who had a strong political base there. (ii) Marker C represents Bihar, the home state of former Deputy Prime Minister Jagjivan Ram, a prominent Dalit leader and freedom fighter. (iii) Marker B represents West Bengal, particularly the Naxalbari area in northern West Bengal, where the Naxalite movement was born in 1967 and remained most active. (iv) Marker D represents a state — likely Rajasthan or another north Indian state — where Congress was completely shut out in the 1977 Lok Sabha elections following the anti-Emergency wave.
questions.solution_hindi: (i) A = उत्तर प्रदेश (चौधरी चरण सिंह से संबंधित), (ii) C = बिहार (जगजीवन राम से संबंधित), (iii) B = पश्चिम बंगाल (नक्सली सबसे अधिक सक्रिय), (iv) D = वह राज्य जहाँ कांग्रेस को 1977 में कोई सीट नहीं मिली।

questions.text: दिया गया कार्टून गठबंधन की सरकारों के युग से संबंधित है। कार्टून का अध्ययन कीजिए और निम्नलिखित प्रश्नों के उत्तर दीजिए : (1+1+2=4) (i) 'रथ यात्रा' का प्लेकार्ड थामे हुए नेता को पहचान कर उसका नाम लिखिए। (ii) किस राजनीतिक पार्टी ने 'रथ यात्रा' का आयोजन किया था ? (iii) कार्टून में दिखाए गए किन्हीं दो प्रधानमंत्रियों को पहचान कर उनके नाम लिखिए जिन्होंने गठबंधन की सरकारों का नेतृत्व किया था।
questions.text_english: The given cartoon is related to the era of coalition governments. Study the cartoon and answer the questions that follow : (1+1+2=4) (i) Identify and name the leader who is holding the placard 'Rath Yatra'. (ii) Which political party organised the 'Rath Yatra' ? (iii) Identify and name any two Prime Ministers shown in the cartoon who led the coalition governments.

sub_questions.text: 'रथ यात्रा' का प्लेकार्ड थामे हुए नेता को पहचान कर उसका नाम लिखिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Identify and name the leader who is holding the placard 'Rath Yatra'.

key_points: L.K. Advani

sub_questions.solution: The leader holding the 'Rath Yatra' placard in the cartoon is L.K. Advani. He led the famous Rath Yatra in 1990 from Somnath to Ayodhya to mobilise support for the Ram Janmabhoomi movement.

sub_questions.text: किस राजनीतिक पार्टी ने 'रथ यात्रा' का आयोजन किया था ?
sub_questions.text_english: Which political party organised the 'Rath Yatra' ?

key_points: Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)

sub_questions.solution: The Rath Yatra was organised by the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). The 1990 Rath Yatra, led by L.K. Advani, was a major political and religious campaign that had significant consequences for Indian politics, including the fall of V.P. Singh's government.

sub_questions.text: कार्टून में दिखाए गए किन्हीं दो प्रधानमंत्रियों को पहचान कर उनके नाम लिखिए जिन्होंने गठबंधन की सरकारों का नेतृत्व किया था।
sub_questions.text_english: Identify and name any two Prime Ministers shown in the cartoon who led the coalition governments.

key_points: V.P. Singh — led the National Front coalition government (1989–1990).
H.D. Deve Gowda — led the United Front coalition government (1996–1997).

sub_questions.solution: Two Prime Ministers visible in the cartoon who led coalition governments are V.P. Singh, who headed the National Front Government from 1989 to 1990, and H.D. Deve Gowda, who led the United Front Government from 1996 to 1997. Other acceptable answers include Chandra Shekhar (1990-91), P.V. Narasimha Rao (1991-96, minority government), or I.K. Gujral (1997-98), all of whom led coalition or minority governments during this era.

questions.solution: Answers to sub-questions: (i) L.K. Advani, (ii) BJP, (iii) Any two of V.P. Singh, H.D. Deve Gowda, Chandra Shekhar, or I.K. Gujral.

questions.text: (क) भारत और रूस के संबंधों का इतिहास आपसी विश्वास और साझे हितों का इतिहास है। किन्हीं तीन उपयुक्त तर्कों द्वारा कथन का समर्थन कीजिए। अथवा (ख) सोवियत संघ के विघटन के बाद शॉक थेरेपी के किन्हीं तीन प्रभावों का विश्लेषण कीजिए।
questions.text_english: (a) The history of relations between India and Russia is a history of trust and shared interests. Support the statement with any three appropriate arguments. OR (b) Analyse any three effects of shock therapy after the disintegration of the Soviet Union.

sub_questions.text: भारत और रूस के संबंधों का इतिहास आपसी विश्वास और साझे हितों का इतिहास है। किन्हीं तीन उपयुक्त तर्कों द्वारा कथन का समर्थन कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: The history of relations between India and Russia is a history of trust and shared interests. Support the statement with any three appropriate arguments.

key_points: Military cooperation: Russia has been India's largest arms supplier for decades, helping build India's defence capabilities.
UN support: The Soviet Union used its veto power multiple times in the UN Security Council to support India on issues like Kashmir.
Economic partnership: The 1971 Indo-Soviet Treaty of Peace, Friendship and Cooperation provided a strategic framework for bilateral cooperation.
Shared strategic interests: Both countries share a vision of a multipolar world and opposition to US unilateralism.

sub_questions.solution: The Indo-Russian relationship is indeed built on deep mutual trust and converging interests, as evidenced by three strong arguments. First, defence cooperation has been the bedrock of the relationship. The Soviet Union and later Russia have been India's most reliable arms suppliers, providing advanced military technology including MiG aircraft, T-90 tanks, and nuclear submarines under the Akula-class lease. Second, diplomatic solidarity at the United Nations has consistently demonstrated Russian support for India. The Soviet Union used its veto in the UN Security Council on multiple occasions to shield India from international pressure, notably during the 1971 Bangladesh war when it vetoed resolutions critical of India. Third, the 1971 Treaty of Peace, Friendship and Cooperation created a long-term institutional framework for the relationship. Under this treaty, both nations committed to mutual support if either faced external aggression, providing India strategic security during the Cold War. These pillars of trust have endured into the contemporary era, making Russia a unique strategic partner for India.

sub_questions.text: सोवियत संघ के विघटन के बाद शॉक थेरेपी के किन्हीं तीन प्रभावों का विश्लेषण कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Analyse any three effects of shock therapy after the disintegration of the Soviet Union.

key_points: Economic collapse: Rapid privatisation led to the collapse of state industries and created mass unemployment.
Rise of oligarchs: State assets were sold at throwaway prices, leading to the emergence of a small group of powerful business oligarchs.
Social hardship: Withdrawal of state subsidies on food, healthcare, and housing caused severe hardship for ordinary citizens.
Political instability: Economic crisis fuelled social unrest and political instability across post-Soviet states.

sub_questions.solution: Shock therapy, the rapid transition from a communist command economy to a free-market capitalist economy, had devastating consequences for the post-Soviet states. First, it led to the collapse of the existing industrial structure. When state enterprises were abruptly privatised without the necessary legal and institutional framework of a market economy, most collapsed, causing GDP to fall dramatically and creating widespread unemployment. Workers who had never experienced joblessness suddenly found themselves without income or social safety nets. Second, shock therapy gave rise to a new class of super-wealthy oligarchs. In Russia particularly, state assets worth billions of roubles were sold at negligible prices to well-connected individuals during 'voucher privatisation'. This created extreme wealth inequality where a handful of individuals controlled vast industries while the majority of citizens lived in poverty. Third, the removal of state subsidies on basic necessities like food, medicine, and housing caused enormous hardship for ordinary people. Life expectancy in Russia dropped, poverty rates soared, and social services collapsed — outcomes that were far worse than what reformers had anticipated.

questions.solution: This question has two internal choice options. Answers are provided under sub_questions (a) and (b).

questions.text: (क) वैश्विक राजनीति के किन्हीं तीन पर्यावरणीय सरोकारों की व्याख्या कीजिए जिनका समाधान किसी एक देश की सरकार अकेले दम पर नहीं कर सकती। अथवा (ख) 'साझी परन्तु अलग-अलग जिम्मेदारियों' के सिद्धांत की व्याख्या कीजिए।
questions.text_english: (a) Explain any three environmental concerns in global politics which no single government can address. OR (b) Explain the principle of 'Common but Differentiated Responsibilities'.

sub_questions.text: वैश्विक राजनीति के किन्हीं तीन पर्यावरणीय सरोकारों की व्याख्या कीजिए जिनका समाधान किसी एक देश की सरकार अकेले दम पर नहीं कर सकती।
sub_questions.text_english: Explain any three environmental concerns in global politics which no single government can address.

key_points: Climate change and global warming require collective reduction of greenhouse gas emissions by all nations.
Depletion of the ozone layer needs international cooperation to phase out CFCs globally.
Biodiversity loss and deforestation transcend national borders and require multilateral conservation agreements.
Ocean pollution and over-fishing of international waters require global regulatory frameworks.

sub_questions.solution: Three major environmental concerns in global politics that require collective international action are as follows. First, climate change and global warming are the most critical. Greenhouse gas emissions from any country affect the atmosphere globally. Rising temperatures, melting ice caps, and extreme weather events threaten every nation, making it impossible for any single state to solve the problem in isolation. The Paris Agreement (2015) represents multilateral recognition of this shared challenge. Second, depletion of the ozone layer illustrates the transboundary nature of environmental damage. Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) used in refrigerants and aerosols by industries in some countries destroy the ozone layer over the entire planet, increasing ultraviolet radiation exposure worldwide. The 1987 Montreal Protocol was a landmark multilateral response. Third, the loss of biodiversity and destruction of global commons such as rainforests and ocean ecosystems cannot be addressed by any nation alone. The Amazon rainforest in Brazil, for example, is a global carbon sink whose deforestation affects the entire planet's climate. Protecting such ecosystems demands international funding, treaties, and cooperation.

sub_questions.text: 'साझी परन्तु अलग-अलग जिम्मेदारियों' के सिद्धांत की व्याख्या कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Explain the principle of 'Common but Differentiated Responsibilities'.

key_points: All countries share the common responsibility to protect the global environment.
However, developed nations bear a greater historical responsibility for current environmental degradation due to their earlier industrialisation.
Therefore, developed countries should bear more of the financial and technological burden of environmental protection.
Developing countries should be allowed flexibility and additional time to meet environmental standards without compromising their development goals.

sub_questions.solution: The principle of Common but Differentiated Responsibilities (CBDR) is a cornerstone of international environmental law, first clearly articulated at the 1992 Rio Earth Summit. The principle has two components. The 'common' part acknowledges that all countries share a collective responsibility to protect the global environment from damage. Since the Earth's atmosphere, oceans, and biodiversity are shared by all humanity, every nation has an obligation to contribute to their protection. The 'differentiated' part recognises a fundamental inequality: developed nations industrialised first and have historically contributed far more to environmental degradation through greenhouse gas emissions, resource exploitation, and pollution. Therefore, they bear a greater moral, financial, and technological responsibility to address these problems. Developing countries like India and China, which are still industrialising to lift their populations out of poverty, are given greater flexibility and are not held to the same immediate emission reduction targets. This principle underpins major agreements like the Kyoto Protocol and the Paris Agreement.

questions.solution: This question has two internal choice options. Answers are provided under sub_questions (a) and (b).

questions.text: (क) स्वतंत्रता के तुरंत पश्चात स्वतंत्र भारत के समज आईं किन्हीं तीन प्रमुख चुनौतियों का वर्णन कीजिए। अथवा (ख) 1947 में विभाजन के समय भारत के कई भागों में उत्पन्न सांप्रदायिक हिंसा को कम करने के लिए, महात्मा गांधी के योगदान का वर्णन कीजिए।
questions.text_english: (a) Describe any three major challenges that independent India faced immediately after independence. OR (b) Describe the role played by Mahatma Gandhi to reduce communal violence that erupted in many parts of India at the time of the partition in 1947.

sub_questions.text: स्वतंत्रता के तुरंत पश्चात स्वतंत्र भारत के समक्ष आईं किन्हीं तीन प्रमुख चुनौतियों का वर्णन कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Describe any three major challenges that independent India faced immediately after independence.

key_points: The challenge of national unity — integrating hundreds of princely states and diverse communities into one nation.
The challenge of establishing democracy in a country with widespread poverty, illiteracy, and little democratic tradition.
The challenge of economic development — poverty, hunger, lack of industry, and dependence on colonial economy.
The challenge of managing Partition — the massive refugee crisis and communal violence that accompanied Partition.

sub_questions.solution: Independent India faced three formidable challenges immediately after 1947. The first was the challenge of national unity and territorial integration. British India was a patchwork of directly governed territories and over 500 princely states, each with its own ruler. Integrating these states into the Indian Union without the use of force (except in Hyderabad and Junagadh) was an enormous political achievement, largely accomplished by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel. The second challenge was establishing a functioning democracy in conditions of extreme poverty and widespread illiteracy. Critics doubted whether universal adult franchise could work in such conditions, yet India successfully held its first general elections in 1951-52 with a massive voter turnout. The third challenge was economic development. India inherited a colonial economy characterised by extreme poverty, lack of industrialisation, food insecurity, and dependence on Britain for manufactured goods. Building a modern economy through five-year plans while reducing poverty and inequality was among the most pressing tasks facing the new nation.

sub_questions.text: 1947 में विभाजन के समय भारत के कई भागों में उत्पन्न सांप्रदायिक हिंसा को कम करने के लिए, महात्मा गांधी के योगदान का वर्णन कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Describe the role played by Mahatma Gandhi to reduce communal violence that erupted in many parts of India at the time of the partition in 1947.

key_points: Gandhi undertook fasts unto death to stop communal violence in Calcutta and Delhi.
He personally visited riot-affected areas to restore peace and calm among communities.
He appealed to both Hindus and Muslims to live in brotherhood and opposed the two-nation theory.
His fast in January 1948 compelled the Indian government to release funds owed to Pakistan, helping to reduce inter-community hostility.

sub_questions.solution: Mahatma Gandhi played a pivotal and extraordinary role in reducing the communal violence that engulfed India at the time of Partition in 1947. While millions fled their homes in the largest mass migration in human history, accompanied by horrific violence between Hindus, Muslims, and Sikhs, Gandhi remained a lone apostle of peace. In Calcutta, where riots had broken out, Gandhi undertook a fast unto death in September 1947, refusing to eat until the violence stopped. His fast had a miraculous effect — leaders of both communities came together and pledged to maintain peace, and the violence in Calcutta subsided remarkably quickly, earning Gandhi the description of a 'one-man boundary force' by Lord Mountbatten. In Delhi, Gandhi again undertook a fast in January 1948, this time pressing both communities for reconciliation and urging the Indian government to release funds owed to Pakistan. He personally visited riot-torn areas, staying in Muslim neighbourhoods to demonstrate solidarity. These acts of extraordinary moral courage helped save thousands of lives and ultimately contributed to India's survival as a secular democratic state.

questions.text: (क) 1979 से 1985 तक असम में बाहरी लोगों के विरुद्ध चले आंदोलन के किन्हीं तीन कारणों का विश्लेषण कीजिए। अथवा (ख) क्षेत्रीय आकांक्षाएँ लोकतांत्रिक राजनीति का अविभाज्य अंग हैं। कथन को न्यायसंगत ठहराइए।
questions.text_english: (a) Analyse any three reasons for the movement against outsiders in Assam from 1979 to 1985. OR (b) Regional aspirations are an integral part of democratic politics. Justify the statement.

sub_questions.text: 1979 से 1985 तक असम में बाहरी लोगों के विरुद्ध चले आंदोलन के किन्हीं तीन कारणों का विश्लेषण कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Analyse any three reasons for the movement against outsiders in Assam from 1979 to 1985.

key_points: Large-scale illegal immigration from Bangladesh, which changed the demographic composition of Assam and threatened the cultural and political dominance of the Assamese people.
Economic grievances — migrants were seen as taking away jobs, land, and economic opportunities from the local Assamese population.
Fear of political marginalisation — if immigrants were granted voting rights, the electoral arithmetic would change and native Assamese would lose political power.

sub_questions.solution: The Assam Movement (1979-1985), led by the All Assam Students' Union (AASU), arose from three interconnected causes. First, there was massive illegal immigration from Bangladesh (both before and after 1971) that fundamentally altered Assam's demographic character. The Assamese felt that their language, culture, and identity were being overwhelmed by the growing number of Muslim Bengali migrants, creating an existential cultural threat to the Assamese people. Second, economic resentment played a significant role. Assam is rich in oil, tea, and other resources, yet the economic benefits were seen as flowing out of the state. On top of this, local Assamese felt that migrants were taking jobs, occupying agricultural land, and competing for economic resources, leaving the indigenous population economically marginalised. Third, political fear was a powerful driver of the movement. The fear was that if illegal immigrants were included in electoral rolls and granted voting rights, they would alter election outcomes, leading to the political marginalisation of the Assamese. The perceived government indifference to these concerns radicalised the movement, which was eventually resolved by the Assam Accord of 1985.

sub_questions.text: क्षेत्रीय आकांक्षाएँ लोकतांत्रिक राजनीति का अविभाज्य अंग हैं। कथन को न्यायसंगत ठहराइए।
sub_questions.text_english: Regional aspirations are an integral part of democratic politics. Justify the statement.

key_points: Democracy legitimises the expression of diverse identities and interests, including regional ones.
Regional parties give voice to specific regional aspirations within the democratic framework.
Federalism, a feature of Indian democracy, institutionally accommodates regional aspirations.
Regional movements in India (like the demand for separate states) have been largely resolved through democratic and constitutional means.

sub_questions.solution: The statement that regional aspirations are an integral part of democratic politics is well-justified. In a large, diverse democracy like India, people have distinct regional identities rooted in language, culture, history, and economic interests. Democracy, by its very nature, provides a legitimate space for these diverse voices to be heard. Regional parties such as the DMK in Tamil Nadu, the Akali Dal in Punjab, and the TDP in Andhra Pradesh have effectively channelled regional aspirations into electoral politics, demonstrating that regional sentiment need not be anti-national. India's federal structure institutionally accommodates these aspirations by giving states autonomy in governance. When regional demands were ignored or suppressed, they sometimes escalated into militancy — as seen in Punjab and the Northeast. However, when addressed through dialogue and constitutional means — as with the States Reorganisation Act (1956), the Punjab Accord (1985), and the Assam Accord (1985) — regional grievances were resolved peacefully. This demonstrates that far from being a threat, regional aspirations, when integrated into democratic processes, actually strengthen democratic governance by making it more representative and responsive.

questions.solution: This question has two internal choice options. Answers are provided under sub_questions (a) and (b).
